# Philadelphia 76ers Season Preview | The NBA's Best Team? Or Overrated?

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-06, 35:11. https://youtu.be/gTsfR5PxAMY

## Summary

Josh Lloyd and Mark Fazetta (Locked On Sixers) preview a heavily changed Philadelphia 76ers roster that adds LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. They agree Jaylen Brown faces the hardest fit and the biggest drop in scoring, while LeBron is described as an "offense creator". Josh doubts LeBron's role will change much from past seasons. Embiid enters the season healthy, but Mark expects only about 40 to 45 games from him and LeBron around 65. Nick Nurse is expected to play his starters heavy minutes, and backup center and rebounding are named as the roster's weak spots. Mark projects about 51 to 52 wins, with some early growing pains.

## Rules and methods

- [2:58](https://youtu.be/gTsfR5PxAMY?t=178) Teams with a lot of roster turnover tend to be rocky in year one. It is easier if the main core stays, and adding stars to existing stars has historically been choppy at first.
  > "how often with teams that have a lot of turnover, it can be a little bit rocky in year one"
- [8:24](https://youtu.be/gTsfR5PxAMY?t=504) When stars on a crowded team miss games, the other players get more scoring chances in those games.
  > "So guys will be able to eat in those games that you don't see those guys out there"
- [30:13](https://youtu.be/gTsfR5PxAMY?t=1813) With new anti-tanking measures, season win totals may run lower, so a team could win about five fewer games and still be equally good.
  > "You could easily have five fewer wins and be an equally good team."
- [26:25](https://youtu.be/gTsfR5PxAMY?t=1585) Position labels like point guard are semantics. Look at actual on-ball usage and assist rate instead of the title.
  > "It's not going to be LeBron running it up there 50% of the time running every single play"
